body:
Nevermind all. Thanks for the discussion. It seems that (Linux) distros/packagers have decided to handle this themselves (like [centos/rhel](https://git.centos.org/rpms/python-requests/blob/c7/f/SOURCES/python-requests-system-cert-bundle.patch#_32
), [fedora](https://src.fedoraproject.org/rpms/python-pip/blob/f31/f/dummy-certifi.patch#_12), and [debian/ubuntu](https://salsa.debian.org/debian/python-certifi/blob/b54ed9cb93817fc6789c125fbd9c26dbcff5dcfc/debian/patches/0001-Use-Debian-provided-etc-ssl-certs-ca-certificates.cr.patch#L24)), and [pip will eventually try to document how it is impacted](https://github.com/pypa/pip/issues/6720#issuecomment-538791684).

I'll go [downstream](https://git.centos.org/rpms/rh-python34-python-pip/tree/c7) and submit a patch to solve the particular case that bit my team.

For future consideration to make partial/incremental progress...
```python
try:
  DEFAULT_CA_BUNDLE_PATH = ssl.get_default_verify_paths().cafile if os.stat(ssl.get_default_verify_paths().cafile).st_size > 0 else where()
except:
  DEFAULT_CA_BUNDLE_PATH = where()
```

Or maybe just formalize the platform/distro approach, and have all platforms simply provide a single well known package with a well known api (blacklist that package on pypi?):
```python
try:
  import where from platform-ca-certificates
except:
  import where from certifi
DEFAULT_CA_BUNDLE_PATH = where()
```
Or something to that effect where the hook is provided here, but implementation is downstream. And pip can just explicitly say `verify = certifi.where()` when in bootstrap/install, unless `--cert` is given.

For dealing with platforms that keep the store somewhere other than on disk, maybe look into using the Mozilla approach [here](https://github.com/mozilla/gecko-dev/blob/69f64d87d901fc8abca0a40d77354429e1bb9a51/security/manager/ssl/EnterpriseRoots.cpp#L355).

And don't get too hung up on the (in)security of the approach. By design, the cert verification is already easily subverted by anything/one that can set an environment variable. It's preferred to make things more secure, but no need to rule out potential solutions that are no worse than the current state (IMO).
```sh
echo REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE=eve.pem >/etc/profile.d/all_your_base.sh
```
